gaps: Run reconciliation: the flow ends at the "Reconciliation started" status — no results, failure or empty-result state was built or exercised, so whether a failed precondition (closed accounting period, lost QBO authorization, missing account mappings — KF-9) is ever named to the user could not be evaluated at all.

Upload blocks: Browse fabricates a file and no real input[type=file] exists, so the wrong-file-type, oversize and parse-error states behind the "CSV or XLSX formats, up to 100MB" promise were never reached.

Close (✕): the state map records only "no visible change, no dialog, no navigation" — it does not record whether the control is unwired in the sketch or intentionally silent, so I could not judge it as a genuine dead click (KF-4).

Account to reconcile (?) tooltip: appears only in the recorded tab order ("Any QuickBooks account can be reconcil…"); its popover content and open/close behaviour were never exercised, so the one place that could explain the shared-account rule is unverified.
Automatic retrieval: the card promises an email when a multi-hour pull is ready, but no waiting, notification or long-running state was exercised, so what the user sees during those hours is unknown.

findings.element: "Run reconciliation" primary button — disabled state (header bar)
findings.finding: Whenever the run is blocked the button simply goes disabled with no tooltip, no inline message and no marking of the blocking field, so nothing on screen names which precondition failed.
findings.user_impact: A user who picks PayPal loses the automatic card and the "Upload manually" toggle at the same time and is left with a dead button and no route forward, and in manual mode a user who removes one of three files sees the button switch off with no clue which file is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Attach a persistent blocker list to the button — one line per unmet precondition naming the exact field and the fix ("Integration file missing — upload the Balance change report", "PayPal has no automatic retrieval — upload both files") — and highlight the offending block.

evidence.action: Selected "Great payments for every one (PayPal)" in Integration; separately, in manual mode, filled all three upload blocks and then clicked Remove on one.
evidence.observed: PayPal: automatic card visible=false, "Upload manually" toggle visible=false, Run disabled=true, and nothing on screen explains why the automatic option is gone. Remove: chips 3→2, Run disabled=true again, with no message naming what is now missing.

findings.element: Import method (Integration) select inside the manual panel vs the "Use automatic retrieval" toggle above it
findings.finding: Two separate controls set the same thing and contradict each other — choosing "Automated (recommended)" inside the manual panel clears the upload blocks but leaves the page in the manual panel with the toggle still offering to switch to automatic.
findings.user_impact: The user has told the screen to use automatic retrieval, the upload blocks vanish as if it worked, yet the automatic card is still hidden and Run stays disabled, so they cannot tell which mode is actually active or how to get back to a runnable state.
findings.suggested_fix: Make mode a single source of truth — either drive the panel from the per-card Import method selects and drop the toggle, or have the in-card "Automated" choice actually switch the page back to the automatic card.

evidence.action: Opened the manual panel via "Upload manually", then picked "Automated (recommended)" in the Integration card's Import method select.
evidence.observed: Upload blocks=0 and Run disabled=true, but the automatic card stayed visible=false and the toggle above still read "Use automatic retrieval" — the two controls disagreed about the active mode.

findings.element: "Upload manually" toggle → manual panel (Accounting card Import method defaults to "Automated")
findings.finding: Clicking "Upload manually" does not put the flow in manual mode — it produces a hybrid in which the Accounting side stays "Automated" while only the integration side flips to "Assisted".
findings.user_impact: A user who chose manual upload specifically because the automatic QuickBooks pull is the part they distrust believes they have supplied both sides of the comparison, when in fact the books half is still being pulled automatically and will fail the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Have "Upload manually" set both cards to a manual import method, or rename the toggle and state per-card which side is automatic and which is uploaded.

evidence.action: Clicked "Upload manually" from the default Stripe + automatic state and read back both Import method selects.
evidence.observed: Manual panel visible=true with 2 source cards; Accounting Import method = "Automated" while the Integration side = "Assisted"; Run became disabled=true with no statement of what was missing.

findings.element: Custom start / end date inputs (period section)
findings.finding: The custom range accepts any values with no validation at all — an end date before the start date and a range entirely in the future both pass and leave "Run reconciliation" enabled.
findings.user_impact: The user starts a run over a range that can contain no transactions, gets the same "Reconciliation started" confirmation as a valid run, and only discovers the mistake much later since the automatic pull is advertised as taking hours.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the range on change — block or flag end-before-start and ranges with no elapsed days, and show the error against the date inputs rather than only disabling the button.

evidence.action: With Custom selected, set the end date to 2026-08-01 while the start stayed 2026-08-31; then set the range to 2027-01-01..2027-12-31.
evidence.observed: Hint read "2026-08-31 – 2026-08-01" and later "2027-01-01 – 2027-12-31"; error element count=0 on the page in both cases and Run reconciliation stayed disabled=false.

findings.element: "Upload manually" / "Use automatic retrieval" toggle — return trip
findings.finding: Switching back to automatic silently discards every file already picked, with no warning before and no notice after.
findings.user_impact: A user who flips to the automatic card to re-read the "can take a few hours" copy before committing loses their uploads on the way back and lands on a disabled Run button that, per UX-1, never tells them the files are gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve picked files across mode switches, or warn before discarding them and state plainly that the uploads were cleared when the user returns to manual.

evidence.action: Filled the upload blocks in manual mode, clicked "Use automatic retrieval" (click 2), then clicked "Upload manually" again (click 3).
evidence.observed: Automatic card returned and Run re-enabled (disabled=false); the files already picked were silently discarded, and the manual panel came back empty with no message.
